City council approves riverside solar park after two-year review

The 40-megawatt project will sit on the former Hollis gravel quarry and is expected to supply about 9,000 homes.

By Maria Okafor · September 21, 2026
Share on X Share on Facebook

The city council voted 7–2 on Monday night to approve a riverside solar park, ending a review that began in the autumn of 2024 and drew more than 600 public comments.

The developer, Northbank Renewables, says construction will start next spring and take about fourteen months. Under the agreement, the city will buy a fifth of the park’s output at a fixed price for twenty years.

Advertisement

Councillor Dana Whitfield, who chaired the planning committee, said the quarry was “land nobody could farm and nobody wanted to build on”. The two councillors who voted against the plan cited concerns about a heron colony downstream.

What happens next

The project still needs a grid connection agreement from the regional operator. Northbank expects that decision before the end of the year.

  • Capacity: 40 megawatts across 96,000 panels
  • Site: 62 hectares of the former quarry
  • Construction: spring 2027, about fourteen months

“This is the largest single step the city has taken toward its 2035 target.”

— Mayor Leon Ferris

A public information evening about the construction schedule will be held at the Hollis community centre on October 3.

Topics: Energy, City council

This article was updated on September 22 to correct the park’s capacity.
